subject: paediatrics
title: Trinucleotide Repeats, Fragile X, Marfan and Noonan Syndromes

steps.tx: Dynamic mutations expand unstably across generations, provoking progressively earlier and more severe disease. Disorders driven by **trinucleotide repeat expansion** violate classic stable Mendelian laws through the genetic phenomenon of anticipation, where repeat copy numbers expand during parental gametogenesis. Repeat thresholds determine phenotypic expression, progressing from normal stability to unmethylated premutation carriers, and ultimately to full disease-causing repeat expansions.
steps.say: Trinucleotide repeat expansions are dynamic mutations that enlarge across generations. Genetic anticipation causes successive generations to suffer earlier disease onset and greater severity.

steps.tx: Hypermethylation and transcriptional silencing of the fragile X mental retardation protein causes intellectual disability. As the most common inherited cause of intellectual impairment in males, **Fragile X syndrome** arises from an unstable CGG repeat expansion exceeding two hundred copies in the 5-prime untranslated region of the FMR1 gene on Xq27.3. Massive expansion induces promoter hypermethylation, silencing FMR1 transcription and eliminating FMRP, an essential mRNA-binding translational repressor in neuronal dendrites.
steps.say: Fragile X syndrome is the most common inherited cause of male intellectual disability. More than two hundred CGG repeats silence the FMR1 gene, eliminating FMRP protein.

left.title: FMR1 Premutation (55 to 200 CGGs)
points: Unmethylated FMR1 gene; normal FMRP levels
Prone to expand to full mutation during oogenesis

right.title: FMR1 Full Mutation (>200 CGGs)
points: Moderate to severe intellectual disability in males
Autism spectrum features and attention deficits
Classic dysmorphic craniofacial and testicular signs

steps.tx: Physical manifestations emerge prominently during pubertal maturation under gonadotropic stimulation. Classic post-pubertal stigmata of Fragile X syndrome include **macroorchidism testicular enlargement**, where testicular volume exceeds thirty millilitres measured by orchidometer. Craniofacial features include a long narrow face, prominent forehead, prognathic chin, large everted pinnae, high-arched palate, joint hypermobility, mitral valve prolapse, and stereotypic hand flapping or biting.
steps.say: Post-pubertal boys with Fragile X display striking macroorchidism with testicular volumes over thirty millilitres. Features include a long face, prominent jaw, large ears, and hand flapping.

rows: Long narrow face, prognathism, large ears
Mitral valve prolapse, aortic root dilation

steps.tx: Fibrillin-1 mutations provoke systemic connective tissue laxity and dysregulated transforming growth factor signalling. The autosomal dominant disorder **Marfan syndrome** is caused by heterozygous mutations in the FBN1 gene on chromosome 15q21 encoding fibrillin-1, a primary microfibrillar extracellular matrix protein. Microfibril deficiency causes fragmentation of elastic fibres and loss of TGF-beta sequestration, resulting in excessive TGF-beta signalling and progressive tissue dilatation.
steps.say: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant fibrillin-1 defect causing elastic tissue weakness and excessive TGF-beta signalling. It affects the skeleton, eyes, and ascending aorta.

left.title: Skeletal Manifestations of Marfan
points: Arm span exceeding standing height by >1.05

right.title: Ocular and Cardiovascular Pathology
points: Ascending aortic root aneurysm and dissection
Dural ectasia on lumbosacral magnetic resonance

steps.tx: Progressive aortic root dilatation represents the foremost life-threatening cardiovascular complication. Progressive **aortic dissection risk** in Marfan syndrome stems from cystic medial necrosis of the elastic aortic root. Pharmacological therapy with beta-blockers or angiotensin receptor blockers (losartan) slows aortic enlargement, while elective prophylactic root replacement is indicated when aortic diameter reaches fifty millimetres, preventing catastrophic spontaneous rupture.
steps.say: Cystic medial necrosis causes ascending aortic aneurysms that risk fatal dissection. Beta-blockers and losartan slow aortic expansion; surgical replacement is done at fifty millimetres.

steps.tx: Hyperactivation of the RAS-MAPK intracellular signalling pathway produces phenotypic features mimicking Turner syndrome. The autosomal dominant RASopathy **Noonan syndrome** is caused by gain-of-function mutations in PTPN11 in fifty percent, as well as SOS1, RAF1, and KRAS. Affecting males and females with normal karyotypes (46,XY or 46,XX), it presents with short stature, webbed neck, low posterior hairline, hypertelorism, downward slanting palpebral fissures, and low-set rotated ears.
steps.say: Noonan syndrome is an autosomal dominant RASopathy mimicking Turner syndrome with normal karyotypes. Features include short stature, webbed neck, low ears, and dysplastic pulmonary valve stenosis.

left.title: Noonan Syndrome Cardiovascular
points: Contrast with Turner coarctation of aorta

right.title: Noonan Genitourinary and Haematological
points: Normal karyotype (46,XY in males; 46,XX in females)
Normal female fertility; reduced male fertility

steps.tx: Universal dried blood spot surveillance detects asymptomatic inborn errors before neurological damage occurs. The public health strategy **newborn screening** collects capillary blood onto standardized Guthrie filter paper cards between forty-eight and seventy-two hours of life. Utilizing tandem mass spectrometry, enzyme assays, and fluoroimmunoassays, screening identifies congenital hypothyroidism, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, phenylketonuria, galactosaemia, and sickle cell disorders.
steps.say: Newborn screening uses heel-prick dried blood spots at forty-eight to seventy-two hours to detect treatable disorders like hypothyroidism, adrenal hyperplasia, and phenylketonuria before damage occurs.

rows: Fatal E. coli sepsis and liver failure

steps.tx: Non-directive communication of genetic risk facilitates autonomous family reproductive planning. Professional **genetic counselling** calculates precise recurrence risks based on Mendelian inheritance, parental carrier status, and gonadal mosaicism. Counsellors explain prenatal diagnostic options including chorionic villus sampling at eleven to thirteen weeks, amniocentesis at fifteen to eighteen weeks, and pre-implantation genetic testing during in vitro fertilization.
steps.say: Genetic counselling calculates precise recurrence risks and guides prenatal testing. Options include chorionic villus sampling at eleven weeks, amniocentesis at fifteen weeks, and pre-implantation tests.

right.title: Amniocentesis
points: Amniocyte culture for karyotype and DNA
